Liver biopsy 9 years prior showed macrovesicular steatosis, hepatocyte ballooning, and bridging fibrosis (stage 3), confirming metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Imaging revealed cirrhosis with splenomegaly and varices. Surveillance imaging detected a liver lesion that enlarged over time, eventually leading to a diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient underwent multiple locoregional therapies (alcohol ablation, radiofrequency ablation) while awaiting transplant. Nineteen months later, he received a liver transplant. Pathology of the explanted liver confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma with vascular invasion.
